subject: ent
title: Dysphagia and the oesophagus

steps.tx: **Dysphagia** separates into oropharyngeal (transfer failure: coughing, choking, nasal regurgitation, recurrent pneumonia, seconds after swallow attempt, from stroke, Parkinson, motor neuron and structural Zenker or cricopharyngeal causes) versus oesophageal (transit failure: food sticking retrosternally seconds later, solids versus liquids pattern). Solids only progressive suggests mechanical stricture or cancer; solids and liquids from start with regurgitation and weight loss suggests motility (achalasia, spasm). Intermittent solid impaction in young atopic man is eosinophilic oesophagitis until scoped.
steps.say: Chokes at once is throat transfer; sticks later is oesophagus. Solids only narrows; both phases fail movement.

vis.alt: A diagram comparing oropharyngeal and oesophageal dysphagia based on symptoms, timing, and causes.
vis.caption: Differentiating oropharyngeal (transfer) and oesophageal (transit) dysphagia

steps.tx: **Key point.** Alarm features override functional labels at any age: progressive course, weight loss, anaemia, odynophagia, older onset, vomiting or family cancer need urgent endoscopy and imaging for malignancy (oesophageal adenocarcinoma on Barrett reflux rising, squamous from smoking alcohol). Rings (Schatzki), webs (Plummer Vinson iron deficiency with postcricoid web and cancer risk), strictures (reflux, caustic, radiation), extrinsic compression and candidiasis in immunocompromise (odynophagia dominant) fill benign differentials.
steps.say: Progressive sticking plus weight loss scopes urgently. Iron deficiency web at top is Plummer Vinson.

steps.tx: Oropharyngeal assessment uses speech therapy clinical swallow plus **videofluoroscopy** or FEES endoscopic evaluation defining aspiration (below cords, silent in neuro disease), penetration and which consistencies or manoeuvres are safe. Management treats cause, modifies textures (IDDSI levels), teaches chin tuck or Mendelsohn strategies, and decides oral versus gastrostomy feeding with patient goals; thickening reduces aspiration of thin fluids in selected patterns but does not suit all.
steps.say: Film the swallow to choose textures. Silent aspirators cough at nothing.

steps.tx: **Globus** is persistent lump in throat sensation between meals without dysphagia, odynophagia or weight loss, often reflux and hypervigilance related, diagnosed after normal examination and (when indicated) scope excluding lesions; reassurance with reflux measures and speech therapy tension release treats it. Zenker pharyngeal pouch (through Killian dehiscence in elderly) causes transfer dysphagia, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, gurgling neck swelling and aspiration, confirmed barium swallow, treated endoscopic stapling or open surgery, never blind NG tube or endoscopy force (perforation into pouch).
steps.say: Lump between meals without sticking is globus. Elderly regurgitated undigested food is Zenker pouch: barium first, tubes beware.
